source.title: Pretrained Approximators for Low-Thrust Trajectory Cost and Reachability
source.authors: Zhonghan Zhang; G. Acciarini; Dario Izzo; H. Baoyin; Francesco Topputo

record.tranche_reason: The study tests an analogous scaling pattern in low-thrust trajectory approximators, a new domain rather than language-model pretraining.
record.gate_note: The paper cites language-model scaling work as related context, but those cited results are not this study's results. Its own figures report test-loss sweeps over network parameters and training-set size. Figure values are not numerically stated in the text. Architecture and hyperparameter comparisons are also reported; the architecture test losses are recorded separately below. No compute-optimal parameter/token allocation or small-run extrapolation experiment is reported.
record.test_reason: The study's own sweeps fit test loss against trainable parameters and training samples with a log–log linear law (Eq. 23, R² > 0.96). This is a new non-language regression setting: MLP surrogates for low-thrust trajectory cost. It bears on V5 only.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors report an approximate empirical log–log scaling of test loss with data and parameters, with no saturation in the explored range. They note the fitted behaviour is specific to their pipeline and that universality is beyond scope. They also say data and model-size effects are largely independent, and that hyperparameters (especially learning rate) still matter greatly.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains low-thrust trajectory regression surrogates and measures test prediction loss as parameter count or training-sample count varies; it does not use language-model pretraining, token/compute scaling, or held-out cross-entropy.
record.method_sensitivity: The authors state the fitted scaling behavior is tied to their input features, normalization, and training protocol. Section 5 reports that hyperparameter selection, particularly learning rate, affects predictive performance; it does not report how those choices change the fitted scaling exponents.
record.problems: The scaling-curve coordinates and exact fitted exponents are not stated in the text, only shown in figures; the reported fits are limited to the explored pipeline and low-thrust prediction setting. The study does not test language-model losses, compute-optimal allocation, or extrapolation from small runs to much larger runs.

untested.parts: Image, video, repeated-data, fine-tuning and transfer regimes. The study covers only supervised regression surrogates for trajectory fuel cost, plus an unreported Δt model. No compute axis is tested.
Not tested: no extrapolation from small fits to much larger runs.
Not tested: no compute-optimal allocation. The authors only state that data and model effects are 'largely independent'.
Not tested: no parameter-matched comparison of shapes.
Not tested: no comparison of exponents across setups or fitting methods.

record.verdict_notes: Only Kaplan et al. is cited, as context. Fig. 1 points are best-of-hyperparameter results per architecture, a selection step that may flatter the fit. The study does not state the exponent or how many orders of magnitude the sweeps span, which limits the strength of the V5 support. The Section 7.2 comparison with the external dataset of [35], using 100× more data, is confounded by differences in domain coverage and is not a scaling measurement.

versions.untested_parts: The study uses low-thrust trajectory models, not language models, and does not measure held-out language-model pretraining loss.
No small-run fit is used to predict the loss of substantially larger runs.
No fixed-compute allocation between parameters and training tokens is studied.
Architecture configurations vary depth and width, but the study does not compare architectures at a fixed parameter count.
The study tests parameter- and dataset-size trends only for low-thrust trajectory approximators; it does not test image/video models, repeated data, fine-tuning, or transfer.
No downstream language-model task performance or relation between language-model pretraining loss and downstream tasks is evaluated.
The paper cautions that the fitted behavior is specific to its pipeline, but does not compare fitted exponents or compute-optimal splits across setups or fitting choices.

relationships.condition: Low-thrust Δv regression MLPs, loss versus trainable parameters or versus training-sample count, within the explored ranges
relationships.reason: Log–log linear fits with R² > 0.96 and no saturation observed in either sweep (r1, r2). Values are from figures only.
relationships.display_finding: Both parameter and sample-size sweeps yielded log-log linear fits with R²>0.96 and no observed saturation.

relationships.condition: Increasing depth at fixed width, on the 100k-sample subset
relationships.reason: Loss stops falling as parameters grow through depth. Width 8: 0.072 to 0.070 over 3–9 layers (r4–r7). Width 128: 0.003 at 5–9 layers (r25–r27). So the parameter law depends on how parameters are added or on a data bottleneck.
relationships.display_finding: At width 8, loss changed only from 0.072 to 0.070 across 3–9 layers, while at width 128 it remained 0.003 across 5–9 layers.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Low-thrust fuel-consumption approximation, varying model size or training dataset size under this paper's pipeline
reader_labels.reason: The authors report approximately linear log–log test-loss trends with R² above 0.96 and no observed saturation in the tested ranges (r1–r2). This supports the pattern in this tested non-language setting, not its universality.
